rationale: Perm is a tiny, recursion-heavy permutation-sort benchmark dominated by small integer-arithmetic and comparison-heavy functions, so SUB gets the highest SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights: integer substitution obscures the arithmetic core at negligible runtime/size cost and near-zero correctness risk on purely integer code. BCF and FLA are kept at moderate weights — they add meaningful control-flow confusion against the recursive backtracking structure, but their runtime and size costs are non-trivial and flattening carries the highest correctness risk (loop/recursion restructuring), so they are favored only where SecurityGain/DiversityGain dominate. SPLIT is cheap and composes well with FLA/BCF, earning a solid mid weight with minimal cost dimensions. IBR, ICALL, and IGV are downweighted because Perm has few indirect-call targets, few globals, and a small branch topology, so their diversity payoff is limited while each adds dispatch overhead and mild correctness risk; they remain enabled at low-to-moderate weights for layered diversity rather than disabled outright, keeping total runtime and size overhead acceptable for this workload.
